newsitem.title: GHANA: Gold Fields Ghana to go ahead with new mine.
newsitem.headline: Gold Fields Ghana to go ahead with new mine.

text.p: Gold Fields Ghana Ltd is to launch the initial phase of an open cast mining project in Tarkwa, southwest Ghana, after getting the go-ahead from the board, Managing Director Helgo Kahle said.

"Since last Friday (when the board met) it has been switched over to a live project. We are now soliciting tenders, placing orders and doing the necessary on the site to get the project going," Kahle told Reuters in an interview.
In its first phase the mine will produce 120-130,000 ounces annually by the end of 1997.
"This is the most exciting mining project on now. We are the second biggest resource in Ghana after Ashanti Goldfields," Kahle said.
The intial phase is based on mining 142 million short tons of ore at an average head grade of 0.037 ounces per ton and a stripping ratio of 2.25.

The plan, subject to a further feasibility study, is to build up ore production and the heap leach processing rate progressively to 8 million short tons per year with an annual production of 230,000 ounces by 2000.
Proven reserves are 324 million tons of ore at 0.040 ounces per ton (almost 13 million ounces of gold). The lifespan of the mine is about 25 years.
Expected capital cost is $125 million excluding inflation and contigencies and the average cash cost over the first five years is expected to be $210 per ounce.
Financing arrangements were not immediately known. "Later this year we are going to the financing communities to present the project," said Kahle.
Gold Fields Ghana took management control and 85 percent of shares of an existing underground mine and a 268 square km concession near Tarkwa in July 1993.
Ghana's government has a 10 percent holding and Crescent Mining Finance Ltd of Canada a five percent stake.
This week Gold Fields Ghana's board published its results for the 1995/96 financial year, which ended on June 30.
The company milled 287,370 tons of ore against 229,558 tons in 1994/95, yielding 47,651 ounces of gold compared with 39,769 in 1994/95, the operating results and income statement showed.
Profit after tax was $1,726,000 compared to $956,000 in 1994/95.
Improved profitability followed a significant increase in tons milled offset by high real wage increases, declining grades and increasing operating depths, the statement said.
Proven and probable reserves total 690,000 tons at 0.31 ounces per ton. Exploration for new reserves in the underground mines had been largely unsuccessful, the statement said.
Ghana produced over 1.5 million ounces of gold last year, of which Ashanti Goldfields produced about two-thirds.
